question: Are the bronzes cast from Degas's wax figures after his death truly works by Degas?
answer: Yes. Every form in them is his: the Hébrard foundry cast them in editions from moulds of his own waxes and clays soon after he died in 1917. Bronze preserves shapes the fragile originals were already losing. Without the casts, few would ever see his sculpture, and many figures would be crumbled wax.
move: Whichever side you took, it turns on whether choosing the material is part of art.
ask: When I give someone credit for a result, who actually made the choices and did the work?
counterpoint: No. Degas modelled in wax and clay, exhibited only one sculpture, and never had any cast in bronze. Choosing a material, a surface and an edition size are artistic decisions, and he made none of them. Surviving waxes show colour, fabric and texture that bronze flattens. A cast he never approved records his forms, not his finished work.
source: National Gallery of Art, Degas sculpture catalogue
reference: Suzanne Glover Lindsay, Daphne S. Barbour & Shelley G. Sturman, Edgar Degas Sculpture, National Gallery of Art, Washington, 2010
